thread:
incident-bot: P1 page created for CypherCore - customer-reported token spike and billing alert on their VPC/dedicated pool. paging on-call: @sam_oncall

sam_oncall: viewing alerts now. Pager shows sudden 3x token consumption on their dedicated pool since 04:06 UTC. Errors? logs?

maria_sre: seeing large influx of requests from cyphercore-prod-vpc, but requests themselves look normal. Token counts are ~3x higher than expected for identical prompts.

kevin_support: CypherCore is very concerned — they opened a ticket about unexpected invoice growth. Provided sample payloads that previously counted ~120 tokens now returning 360 tokens.

jess_prod: likely tokenizer/encoding mismatch. We pushed a tokenizer patch for a different model last week into a shared wheel; possible the dedicated pool is loading an incompatible tokenizer binary.

ryan_engineer: looking at model runtime logs for cyphercore-dedicated-2. Trace shows model flavor: open-llama-13b, tokenizer version: 2025.02 vs expected 2024.11.

sam_oncall: confirm scope — is this affecting other tenants on the same cluster?

maria_sre: isolation check: dedicated pool is isolated to CypherCore. No other tenants show spike. So impact is customer-scoped but severe for them (billing + rate limits).

incident-bot: Incident P1 | cyphercore-tokenizer-inflation | severity: high | SLA impacted: billing & rate limits | responders: @sam_oncall, @maria_sre, @ryan_engineer

nora_bizops: looping in revenue ops. We need preliminary estimate of overbilled tokens to prepare credits.

anna_ops: can we throttle or route them to a fallback model variant with the verified tokenizer while we fix their pool?

ryan_engineer: yes. Suggest steps: 1) set routing policy to route CypherCore traffic to cyphercore-fallback (same model architecture, pinned tokenizer 2024.11) 2) restart dedicated pool nodes to ensure new tokenizer binary not loaded 3) run reconciliation job to compute delta tokens for billing credit.

sam_oncall: doing step 1 now — applying temporary routing rule to direct traffic to fallback variant. ETA ~2 min.

maria_sre: implementing a read-only lock on the pool to prevent new model binary pulls while we inspect.

kevin_support: told CypherCore support contact (Alex) that we're routing to fallback and investigating; asked for a sample of affected prompts and timestamps. They responded with 10 samples.

jess_prod: past diff shows our tokenizer wheel changed byte order for multi-byte whitespace handling; that can inflate token counts for certain encodings (utf-8 vs legacy encoder). If dedicated pool picked up the new wheel, tokenization differences would explain 2-4x counts.

ryan_engineer: confirmed: cyphercore-dedicated-2 /var/lib/models/tokenizer/wheel shows version 2025.02. Our verified version for that customer should be 2024.11 (due to enterprise pinning in their onboarding manifest). Looks like a config drift in the private control plane sync.

sam_oncall: root cause candidate: control plane sync mistakenly flagged pool as eligible for latest tokenizer rollout. Need rollback.

maria_sre: rollback plan: 1) mark pool to pin tokenizer=2024.11 in control plane 2) force model restart to load pinned tokenizer 3) verify token counts on sample payloads 4) once validated, schedule a billing reconciliation job.

ryan_engineer: performing pin now and restarting model processes. Restart logs:

```
Restarting model worker on cyphercore-dedicated-2 node-3
Loaded tokenizer version: 2024.11
Self-check sample: prompt "Summarize Q3 revenue" -> tokens: 122 (expected 120)
Health: OK
```

kevin_support: CypherCore acknowledged routing to fallback and appreciates rapid response. They asked for a rollback ETA. I said ~30 mins to validate then provide credit estimate.

nora_bizops: needs preliminary token delta estimate ASAP. Can someone run a quick scan of the last 24h usage for that tenant and compute apparent multiplier?

anna_ops: running a query against usage store filtered by tenant_id=cyphercore for last 24h. Quick result: nominal tokens 18M expected; observed tokens 54M -> multiplier ~3.0.

nora_bizops: noted. We'll prepare provisional credit for 36M tokens at hosted rate equivalent. Keep in mind dedicated pricing different; but we need an internal placeholder.

sam_oncall: validating sample inputs against live endpoint on fallback — token counts match historical expectations. Good.

maria_sre: monitoring metrics: inbound request rate stable; token-per-request metric dropped back to expected. No further increase.

ryan_engineer: action items: create a postmortem note (will draft), add an automated guard to prevent tokenizer wheel rollouts to pinned dedicated pools, and create a reconciliation job to compute exact overcharge.

incident-bot: On-call handoff scheduled in 40 minutes to @maria_sre (primary) -> @ryan_engineer (secondary) remains on stand-by.

kevin_support: going to send CypherCore a short incident update: what happened, what we did (routing to fallback, pinned tokenizer, restart), ETA for bill reconciliation.

jess_prod: also open a fix PR to ensure control plane respects per-tenant pinning overrides at apply-time (fail if conflict). Add a diagnostic to the sync logs to show override violations.

nora_bizops: after reconciliation, we should offer CypherCore a one-time invoice adjustment plus a 30% service credit for operational disruption. Recommend legal check but that is a good starting offer.

anna_ops: reconciliation job completed draft: compares tokens billed per request against tokens recomputed with pinned tokenizer across last 7 days, flags requests >1.2x multiplier. Produces CSV for billing ops.

sam_oncall: moving to monitor state. Root cause: control plane rollout allowed tokenizer update to hit tenant-dedicated pool that was supposed to be pinned -> caused tokenization inflation and overbilling.

maria_sre: assigning follow-ups: - jess_prod to PR fix control plane enforcement - ry an_engineer to finalize reconciliation and export - anna_ops to validate additional dedicated pools for drift - nora_bizops to prepare customer comms/credit proposal.

ryan_engineer: reconciliation run complete: exact observed delta for last 24h = 35,423,812 tokens. Exported CSV uploaded to S3 at s3://redwood-incidents/cyphercore/1915001234/reconciliation.csv (internal link).

kevin_support: updated customer: initial report + mitigation summary + promise of credit estimate within 4 hours. They asked to preserve logs for compliance.

maria_sre: marking incident as mitigated (routing fallback + pinned tokenizer + restarts done). Will keep incident open for billing reconciliation and postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident state updated -> mitigated (customer traffic routed to verified tokenizer). Severity downgraded to P2 for billing reconciliation.

nora_bizops: preparing customer-facing summary and credit offer. Will share draft in #customer-commms channel and request approvals.

sam_oncall: final note: immediate customer impact contained and isolated to CypherCore's dedicated pool. Follow-ups required to prevent recurrence. Good job team. :thumbsup:

anna_ops: adding retrospective check: scan all dedicated pools for tokenizer version != pinned version and alert on drift.

jess_prod: PR opened: control-plane: enforce pinning on rollout; add rolling-window check to abort if pool is pinned. Requesting review from @maria_sre.

ryan_engineer: I'll draft the postmortem and include timeline + estimated customer cost + remediation steps. Want to get it out within 48h.

kevin_support: closing loop with CypherCore — will request acknowledgement that routing to fallback resolved their immediate billing spike.

nora_bizops: once we confirm reconciliation numbers, we'll process invoice adjustment and 30% service credit proposal.

maria_sre: incident closed for active mitigation. Leaving this thread open for billing and postmortem items.

sam_oncall: handing off final watch to @maria_sre. Thanks everyone.

maria_sre: taking watch. Will post postmortem link here when ready.
